newsitem.title: ALBANIA: ALBANIA CANCELS SPORTS EVENTS IN WAKE OF RIOTS.
newsitem.headline: ALBANIA CANCELS SPORTS EVENTS IN WAKE OF RIOTS.

text.p: The Albanian government has banned all public sports events following the wave of unrest sparked by the collapse of pyramid savings schemes, the state secretary for sports said on Wednesday.
Marjeta Zace told Reuters that the interior ministry had suggested that all sports events should be postponed until the situation returned to normal.
"I spoke with the interior minister today...and it was decided that (soccer matches) should not be held this week because the situation is still not calm," Zace said.
"Next week I hope we can resume the programme," she added.
Soccer matches were not held last week because of violent demonstrations around the country, during which protestors burned several government buildings, set up road blocks and stoned police.
More demonstrations are scheduled for later this week.

The daily newspaper Gazeta Shqiptare reported on Wednesday that Mario Kempes, the former Argentine soccer international who is coach of Albania's Lushnje team, had asked for permission to leave the country until calm returned.
Almost everyone in Albania has been affected by the recent collapse of several immensely popular pyramid savings schemes.
